skill.name: scoop-ui-refactor

content.value_statement: Scoop UI updates can spread across feed, globe, research, and theme files. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused refactor workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides review of Scoop home, globe, research, and global CSS surfaces.
Prioritizes preserving view modes, filters, research results, and modals.
Defines denser home feed layout goals with compact story and contact sections.
Improves globe selection with country focus, source counts, top sources, and reset actions.
Structures the research workspace with query, Brief, Flow, and sidebar patterns.
Documents snap-scroll behavior for wheel, touch, and keyboard navigation.
limitations: Applies to the Scoop frontend project structure described in the skill.
Does not include executable scripts or automated refactor commands.
Does not resolve pre-existing lint failures noted by the author.
Requires manual UI verification after code changes.

use_cases.title: Refresh the Home Feed
use_cases.description: Compress story layout, keep controls visible, and preserve existing feed actions during a Scoop UI refactor.

use_cases.title: Improve Country Exploration
use_cases.description: Clarify globe selection flow with focus context, source counts, top sources, and a visible reset path.

use_cases.title: Standardize Refactor Checks
use_cases.description: Use the listed checks to verify view modes, filters, research rendering, modals, and snap-scroll behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Refactor Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Scoop UI refactor skill to review the listed frontend surfaces. Propose a small plan that preserves existing features.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor the Home Feed
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate layout update for the main feed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor the Scoop home feed for better density. Preserve view modes, filters, modals, bookmarks, likes, and favorites.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Globe Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced UX update for the globe workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve the Scoop globe view. Add clearer country focus, source counts, top sources, and a reset action without using emoji.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Snap Scroll Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced interaction work with regression checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement feed snap-scroll for wheel, touch, and arrow keys. Keep the global header accessible and verify existing feed actions still work.

output_examples.input: Refactor the Scoop home layout for higher density.
output_examples.output: A focused edit plan and implementation that reduces empty space, keeps controls visible, and preserves existing feed actions.

output_examples.input: Improve the globe view selection experience.
output_examples.output: Updated UX guidance that emphasizes country focus, source counts, top sources, reset controls, and removal of flag emoji.

output_examples.input: Check snap-scroll behavior after a feed refactor.
output: Source filters and modals still work.
Wheel, touch, and arrow key snap-scroll behavior remains usable.

best_practices: Start by reviewing the listed frontend files and current user workflows.
Preserve existing actions before changing density, layout, or scroll behavior.
Separate pre-existing lint failures from issues introduced by the refactor.
anti_patterns: Do not remove filters, modals, bookmarks, likes, favorites, or research behavior.
Do not hide the global header during feed snap-scroll transitions.
Do not introduce emoji in UI strings, logs, or documentation.

faq.question: What project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for the Scoop news platform frontend and its documented project structure.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and file targets, but it does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it fix existing lint errors?
faq.answer: No. The skill notes existing lint failures and treats them as separate from snap-scroll layout work.

faq.question: What should remain unchanged?
faq.answer: View modes, filters, research results, modals, bookmarks, likes, and favorites should continue to work.

faq.question: Why does it ban emoji?
faq.answer: The workflow requires replacing emoji with icons or labels across UI strings, logs, and documentation.
